newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate moves up on low demand.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate moves up on low demand.

text.p: Croatia's average lending rate jumped 80 basis points to 11.8 percent on Tuesday despite a cut in the interbank call money rate amid very low demand.
Settlements totalled only 17.2 million kuna against 120 million on offer. Fresh borrowings accounted for 12.2 million.
The rest were one-week funds, rolled over at 10 percent by insurers and at 12.5 percent by banks.
The weighted call money rate eased 50 basis points to 10.5 percent.
The central bank's kuna midrates for Wednesday eased to 5.8907 against the dollar and firmed slightly to 3.5634 versus the German mark. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
